x: The race resulted in a win for Dabbs with Flanagan 2nd and Boreham 3rd. The winner's time of 4.39 was a long way behind Ray Tooby's record of 4.28.

Can we look to Baulch, Flanagan, Dabbs, Hooper, Biscoe, Newell and Hallowell to mention but a few to instil the enthusiasm, or are we to continue in the same groove until the might of Belgrave wanes like the Roman Empire of old.

Though the troopers had the individual winner, junior Flanagan was first man home for the club in 2nd place. Part of the race was apparently run through enemy territory during the course of which we collected some casualties.

Charlie Walker took the lead quickly, with Baulch, Bagnall and Flanagan on his heels. Round the first lap of the Common, Flanagan went to the front but was not allowed to keep his nose ahead for long.

Flanagan ran very well to finish first, beating Gilham of the Bank by 15 sec. They were followed by three Bank runners but as the next six were all Belgravians, the balance was tipped slightly in our favour and we won by one point - a very fair result.
However, Flanagan ran extremely well to gain 40th place, but one wonders how much better he would perform with a less loping action; his style was definately unsuited to the going.

9th George Flanagan Not deterred by the big gap ahead with no-one in sight, George set about his task in workmanlike manner and by steady running closed the two-minute gap with Sheffield by no less than 60 sec. and pulled back fifteen seconds on T.V.H. the leaders.

George Flanagan, one of our youngest team members, had the difficult leg from Mitcham to Purley.
